clue.text: Two halves of short Greek aristocrat

indicators.note: of is read as made of: the two halves of the shortened word, with the joining word between them
short means the word loses its final letter, here dropping the K at its end

parts.note: taken as written
two halves of something are its first half and its second half, so the word joining them is the little word and

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about part of a shortened Greek nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts GREEK to GREE; its two halves are GR and EE, and 'Two halves' read as the halves joined by AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank, and by extension any high-ranking aristocrat.

clue.text: Have trouble breathing when doctor's round

indicators.note: round says the doctor's letters go around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor; the 's reads as 'is'
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A patient struggles for breath while the doctor is making house calls.
explanation.definitionFit: To pant or catch the breath sharply is a struggle to breathe.

clue.text: Character left on water taxi after landing here?

parts.note: an air is a manner or demeanour, a person's character as it shows
port is the left side of a ship, the nautical word for left

explanation.surface: A water taxi seems to be dropping someone off on the left-hand bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taxi' is a verb here: planes taxi along the ground after landing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft roll along runways and aprons to their gates after touching down at an aerodrome.

clue.text: Women in a fix try to find water

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a fix is an addict's dose

explanation.surface: Women in difficulties set out to search for water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fix' looks like a predicament but is a drug addict's dose.
explanation.definitionFit: Divining with a forked rod is the traditional way to search for underground water.

clue.text: Did test engineer need to cover up giant screen?

indicators.note: to cover says the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece
to engineer is to contrive or rework, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: IMAX is the brand of very large cinema screens

explanation.surface: Did an engineer test the need to hide a huge cinema screen?
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineer' is the anagram signal, not a person; 'up' turns the screen brand round in this down clue, and 'to cover' wraps the rearranged letters round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have inspected or checked something closely is to have put it through a test.

clue.text: Dubious nugget I cooked with cod fat

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared afresh, reshuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook boasts about a dodgy nugget fried with cod in fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A questionable item of information repeated until it is accepted as true is a dubious nugget.

clue.text: Like the police, being rude?

definitions.meaning: the filth is British slang for the police, so this describes something resembling them
rude here means obscene or smutty

explanation.surface: Is being rude typical of the police?
explanation.walkthrough: 'the filth' is derogatory British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means obscene or indecent, and jokingly also describes something of the police.

clue.text: Wits witter wicked whist whizz?

parts.note: a card is a witty or eccentric person, so cards are wits
to harp on is to witter on about something tediously

explanation.surface: An alliterative string of words about a crafty card-game ace.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler who cheats at card games is a skilled but crooked player, a whizz at whist.

clue.text: Ex-husband following Jesus stuck with new master

parts.note: old means former, an ex

indicators.note: stuck with says one piece is lodged inside the other

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, counts years from the birth of Jesus

explanation.surface: A woman's former spouse has taken up with a new spiritual master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' links: the husband comes after Ex. 'stuck with' lodges N inside AD to give AND.
explanation.definitionFit: An experienced, skilled veteran is a master of the craft.

clue.text: Matted thatch needing clods raked out

indicators.note: out says the letters are thrown out of order, like soil raked about

explanation.surface: A roof's thatch needs the clumps of earth raked out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raked out' reads as a single action, but 'raked' is fodder and 'out' alone signals the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropelike matted locks of hair are a thatch in the slang sense of a head of hair.

clue.text: Wacky small party for eight, perhaps

parts.note: a rowing eight is an example of a crew
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: An eccentric little party is being thrown for eight guests.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a racing rowing boat and its crew.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means crazy or eccentric, just as wacky does.

clue.text: Roof-top's free energy plugged by Government

indicators.note: plugged by says the government piece is stuffed into the other letters

parts.note: to rid is to free
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A rooftop solar scheme promising free energy is being promoted by government.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex line where the two slopes of a pitched roof meet is its top.

clue.text: Doctor dating honest man finally making a little time for love

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered into a new order
finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A doctor going out with a decent man finds a little time for romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief sexual encounter lasting just one evening is a little time spent on love.

clue.text: Maybe all those enjoying Plath toy with her despair

indicators.note: to toy with something is to play about with it, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Sylvia Plath's fans are drawn to her poetry's despair.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of people who read a writer, such as fans of the poet Plath, is her audience.

clue.text: Dear Claude meets expectations, somewhat contrarily

indicators.note: contrarily says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A letter's greeting to Claude says he partly met expectations, but not quite as hoped.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear and highly regarded are synonyms, as in 'my dear and respected colleague'.

clue.text: With poise and short of time, agent goes about his business

definitions.text: With poise and short of time, agent goes about his business

indicators.note: goes about suggests moving around, so the letters are rearranged
short of says the word loses the following piece

explanation.surface: A cool, hurried secret agent carries on with his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of time' takes T from AGENT; 'goes about' then rearranges POISE with AGEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is the business of a secret agent who works coolly against the clock.

clue.text: Testing hearts — jack, maybe ten

parts.note: a jack is an example of a playing card
IO looks like the figures 10

explanation.surface: A card player's hand: hearts, with a jack or perhaps a ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts' looks like the card suit but is the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix and short form refer to the heart, as in exercise or tests of heart function.

clue.text: Come up with ready slogan for oil nimbies?

definitions.meaning: ready is British slang for cash, so this means to pay up
a protest chant telling the oil company Shell to leave the area

explanation.surface: A catchy slogan for local campaigners who oppose oil drilling.
explanation.walkthrough: Nimbies ('not in my back yard') oppose local developments; Shell is an oil company.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay out money, often reluctantly, is to produce the cash needed.

clue.text: Limp is what limits Dorothy, nursing bad back

indicators.note: nursing says the outer letters hold the other piece inside
what limits a word is its boundary letters, the first and last
back says the word is read backwards

parts.note: poor means bad

explanation.surface: Dorothy limps along, coddling a bad back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sagging and floppy is limp, like a wilting flower.

clue.text: Bloom for one with yellow look externally

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow

indicators.note: externally says the look letters sit on the outside, around the other piece

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
and can mean with, as in 'bread and butter'

explanation.surface: A yellow flower that looks like it is blooming outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloom is the actor Orlando Bloom, not a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor Bloom's first name, so Bloom is one person bearing it.

clue.text: Hard work expands support for flower business, as discussed elsewhere

indicators.note: expands says the support word is swelled by having the other letters put inside it

parts.note: a stalk holds up a flower
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A florist's hard work boosts sales of stems, as mentioned elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Conversation about one's job in a social setting is work matters discussed away from the workplace.

clue.text: Extra-loud curly style conservationists insult

indicators.note: extra says one more letter is put into the word

parts.note: an Afro is a hairstyle of tight curls
F is forte, the musical direction for loud
the NT, National Trust, is the British body that conserves historic places

explanation.surface: Heritage campaigners are offended by a very loud, curly hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the UK charity looking after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate slight or offence is an insult.

clue.text: What might identify an Irishman's last work?

definitions.text: What might identify an Irishman's last work?

parts.words: What might identify an Irishman's last work?
parts.note: an Irish accent marks a speaker as Irish, and a sturdy shoe is cobbler's work made on a last, the foot-shaped form shoes are built on

explanation.surface: What might reveal an Irish writer's final piece?
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' reads as final, but it is the cobbler's foot-shaped form.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a strong Irish accent and a heavy decorated leather shoe.

clue.text: Easy way to load baps, piled high

parts.note: baps are soft bread rolls; piled up, one roll sits on another roll
off means high, as meat or milk gone bad

explanation.surface: Bread rolls stacked high make for easy loading.
explanation.walkthrough: Baps are British soft bread rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferries where vehicles drive on and drive off offer a simple loading method.

clue.text: Multiply decimal

definitions.meaning: multiply as an adverb from multiple: many times over, frequently
decimal means based on the number ten

explanation.walkthrough: 'Multiply' looks like the verb but is the adverb from multiple; 'decimal' splits as two words, of ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening many times over is happening frequently.

clue.text: Lose cool picture

definitions.meaning: a photograph, especially a casual one

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to break suddenly under strain, and a quick photograph.

clue.text: Will S's partner put back natural colour?

indicators.note: put back says the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: William Shakespeare's wife was Anne Hathaway, Anne H for short

explanation.surface: Will his partner restore her natural hair colour?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will S' is William Shakespeare, whose wife was Anne Hathaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown dye made from a plant, used on hair and skin, is a natural colouring.

clue.text: Army misfit finally wears dress where there's no-one around

indicators.note: wears says the dress goes around the pieces, as clothing around a body

parts.note: a gown is a dress
a host is an army, as in heavenly host

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An army oddball ends up wearing a dress where nobody can see.
explanation.definitionFit: An abandoned settlement with no remaining inhabitants is a place with nobody about.

clue.text: In gym class, repeated exercises by good pupil

indicators.note: in says the pieces are placed inside the gym class letters

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym class

indicators.note: by says the good letter goes beside the exercises

parts.note: rote is learning by repeated drilling

explanation.surface: A teacher's star pupil does drills over and over in gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A person guided and promoted by a mentor is their pupil or disciple.

clue.text: Waterproof the best item of clothing to display biceps?

definitions.text: item of clothing to display biceps?

parts.note: a tank is a watertight container that holds water
top means the best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: Waterproof the finest sleeveless garment for showing off one's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless knitted pullover leaves the upper arms bare, letting muscles show.
